([[Phoenix, Arizona]]) | college = [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] (2017–2018) | highlights = * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2018 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2018]]) * [[Karl Malone Award]] (2018) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]] ([[2017–18 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|2018]]) * First-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] (2018) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 Freshman of the Year]] (2018) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|Pac-12 Tournament]] {{abbr|MOP|Most Outstanding Player}} ([[2018 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2018]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2017]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2017) }} '''Deandre Ayton''' (born July 23, 1998) is a Bahamian [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] in the [[Pac-12 Conference]] in the 2017–18 season. He was a consensus five-star prospect in the Class of 2017, and was selected as a [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]].{{cite web | url = http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm | title = 2017 McDonald’s All-American Game boys rosters announced | work = maxpreps | date = 15 January 2017 | accessdate = 20 February 2017}} ''[[ESPN]]'' analyst [[Jay Williams (basketball)|Jay Williams]] compares Ayton to [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]] and [[Anthony Davis (basketball)|Anthony Davis]].{{cite web |title=Deandre Ayton scouting report: Anthony Davis + Al Horford + David Robinson? |work=ESPN The Next Level |date=May 18, 2018 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5YLiGLQw840 |via=[[YouTube]] }} == Early life == Ayton was born to Alvin and Andrea Ayton. He has four siblings. Ayton was born in [[Nassau, Bahamas]] and moved to [[San Diego|San Diego, California]] in the [[United States]] when he was young.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/08/03/deandrey-ayton-recruiting-2017-top-prospect-bahamas|title=Inside DeAndre Ayton's rise from the Bahamas to 2017's No. 1 prospect|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}} Ayton was first scouted by an Annual Bahamian basketball magazine called The Bahamian Basketball Yearbook.{{Cite web|url=http://www.allbahamian.com|title=The All Bahamian Brand|last=|first=|date=1 May 2007|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=|access-date=}} At the time, Ayton, then a 12-year-old tuba and soccer player, was scouted by The All Bahamian Brand was visiting Bahamas Academy High School, a tiny private school then located on Wulff Road in Nassau. The scouts came when Ayton was at band practice, rather than basketball practice, but were impressed by his 6'5" frame. ==High School career== Ayton attended Balboa City School in San Diego, California and started on the varsity basketball team for two years. As a sophomore in 2014–15, Ayton led Balboa to a 17-14 record, averaging 21 points, 16 rebounds and 3.8 blocks per game. He racked up double-doubles in 21 of 22 regular season games. That summer, he averaged 16.5 points, 13.5 rebounds and 2.2 blocks a game for Supreme Court AAU (California) on the Under Armour circuit. He transferred from Balboa City School. As a junior in 2015–16, he elected to transfer to Hillcrest Prep Academy in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] for two more years,{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/13825572/no-1-recruit-deandre-ayton-enrolls-hillcrest-hoops-prep-academy|title=No. 1 recruit Ayton enrolls at Hillcrest Hoops|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/02/04/hillcrest-wants-raise-arizona-hoops-7-1-deandre-ayton/79823230/?from=global&sessionKey=&autologin=|title=Hillcrest wants to raise Arizona hoops with 7-1 DeAndre Ayton|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://hs.utpreps.com/news_article/show/480554|title=S.D. prep basketball’s hidden treasure|first=Don Norcross, Special to the|last=U-T|date=17 February 2015|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}} During this high school year, he became teammates with another top-tier Class of 2017 player in [[Marvin Bagley III]]. Throughout his junior year, Ayton averaged 29.2 points, 16.7 rebounds, 3.8 blocks per game. As a senior in 2016–17, Ayton led Hillcrest to a 33-6 record and national rankings across multiple outlets while averaging 26 points, 15 rebounds and 3.5 blocks. While representing the World Select team, Ayton played at the 2016 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], chipping in with eight points to go along with seven rebounds.{{Cite web|url = http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2016/04/usa-wins-2016-nike-hoop-summit.aspx|title = USA Wins Nike Hoop Summit 101-67|website = www.usab.com|access-date = 2016-04-10}} ===Recruiting=== Ayton was considered the top player in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/player/184253-deandre-ayton|title=DeAndre Ayton, Arizona Wildcats, Center (BK)|website=247Sports|accessdate=9 January 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/blog/ncbrecruiting/on-the-trail/insider/post?id=13964|title=How DeAndre Ayton got to No. 1|date=10 June 2015|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=9 January 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article53500780.html|title=Mustang Madness preview: UK target Ayton ‘as good as it gets’ in high school basketball|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}} In 2015, he was ranked by Scout as the top prospect in all of high school in their "Ultimate 100" list.{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1510205-scout-s-ultimate-100|title=Scout's Ultimate 100|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}} He had narrowed his choices between three schools: Arizona, Kansas and Kentucky. On September 6, 2016, DeAndre committed to play for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]http://m.tucsonnewsnow.com/tusconnewsnow/db_330662/contentdetail.htm?contentguid=b9YHjWDJ{{cite web|url=http://www.kgun9.com/news/local-news/arizona-basketball-lands-no-1-class-of-2017-recruit|title=Arizona Basketball lands No. 1 class of 2017 recruit|first=Mac Colson, The|last=AP|date=7 September 2016|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/video/clip?id=17481403|title=Top basketball prospect Ayton picks Arizona - ESPN Video|publisher=|accessdate=9 January 2018}}, and he signed his letter of intent. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = DeAndre Ayton | position = C | hometown = [[Phoenix, Arizona|Phoenix, AZ]] | highschool = Hillcrest Prep Academy (AZ) | feet = 7 | inches = 0 | weight = 235 | 40 = | commitdate = 09/06/16 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Arizona 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2017 Arizona Basketball Commits | espn ref title = 2017 Arizona Wildcats Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = 2017 Arizona 24/7 Sports Commits | rivals school = arizona | 247 school = Arizona | scout s = 106 | espn schoolid = 12 | scout overall = 5 | rivals overall = 3 | 247 overall = 4 | espn overall = 3 | accessdate = September 6, 2016 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Ayton made his debut with the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|University of Arizona]] on November 10, 2017, recording 19 points, 12 rebounds, and 3 blocks in a 101–67 win over the [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona Lumberjacks]]. His 19 points was 7th most for a Freshman in an Arizona debut. On December 9, 2017, Ayton recorded what was, at the time, a season-high 29 points and 18 rebounds in an 88–82 win over the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. On December 30, 2017, against the in-state rival [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State Sun Devils]], he recorded 19 rebounds, which would be a season-high at the time. On January 20, 2018, against [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], he blocked 6 shots, which tied him for most in Arizona Freshman single game history. He has also recorded 17 20-point games and 23 double-doubles through 34 games.{{Cite web|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/arizona.sidearmsports.com/documents/2017/10/31/2017_18_Arizona_Basketball_Media_Guide_Online_.pdf|title=2017-18 Arizona Media pGuide|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=|access-date=}} On February 23, 2018, a reported [[FBI]] wiretap revealed Arizona's head coach, [[Sean Miller]], allegedly talked with Christian Dawkins (a key figure involved in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]]) to discuss paying Ayton $100,000 to allow him to enter the university, with the monetary situation being dealt with directly to him.http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22559284/sean-miller-arizona-christian-dawkins-discussed-payment-ensure-deandre-ayton-signing-according-fbi-investigation While Miller would not be coaching the next game a day later against [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]], Ayton would still be allowed to play that day as the starting center. In that game, Ayton would record 28 points, 18 rebounds, and 4 blocks in the overtime loss to Oregon. The wiretapped conversation reportedly occurred in 2016, when Ayton was still attending the Hillcrest Prep Academy.https://247sports.com/Article/Sources-Conflicting-information-in-ESPNs-report-involving-Arizona-star-DeAndre-Ayton-coach-Sean-Miller-115594868https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/ncaab/ua/2018/02/26/espn-corrects-report-arizona-basketball-sean-miller-wiretap-call/373594002/https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/01/arizona-sean-miller-deandre-ayton-espn-report On March 3, 2018, after their last regular season home game against California, where he'd record 26 points and a career-high 20 rebounds in a 66–54 win over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]], head coach [[Sean Miller]] honored Ayton, as well as underclassmen [[Rawle Alkins]] and [[Allonzo Trier]], with confirmations that they'd all be entering the [[2018 NBA Draft]] at the end of this season.https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/03/sean-miller-deandre-ayton-arizona-nba-draft On March 9, Ayton would record a career-high 32 points with 14 rebounds in a 78–67 overtime win against UCLA. He'd tie that career-high for points the next day alongside grabbing 18 rebounds in the Pac-12 Championship game against USC, where the Wildcats won 75–61. Ayton would be named the Pac-12 Tournament's Most Outstanding Player during the event. At the end of the regular season, Ayton was named both the Pac-12's Freshman of the Year and Player of the Year, as well as become a member of the All Pac-12 first team and All Pac-12 first team in the Associated Press. He would also be named one of the consensus members of the All-American First Team throughout multiple organizations. Ayton was also one of three freshman to be a part of the All-American First Team, joining [[Marvin Bagley III]] and [[Trae Young]] for the most consensus freshmen First Team members in a season. Following Arizona's upset loss to [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo University]] in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|2018 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament]], Ayton announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he is expected to be a top-tier [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] selection, if not potential #1 draft pick.{{Cite news|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/deandre-ayton-allonzo-trier-declare-nba-draft-arizonas-stunning-loss-045332084.html|title=Deandre Ayton, Allonzo Trier declare for NBA draft after Arizona's stunning loss|access-date=2018-03-16|language=en-US}} On April 26, 2018, it was announced that Ayton had signed with agent Nima Namakian of BDA Sports.https://twitter.com/SBJLizMullen/status/989536537560760320 '''All-time Arizona Freshman Leader Ranks{{Cite web|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/arizona.sidearmsports.com/documents/2017/10/31/2017_18_Arizona_Basketball_Media_Guide_Online_.pdf|title=2017-18 Arizona Media Guide|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|dead-url=|access-date=}}:''' * Total Points -
